description: The CHARIM GeoNode shares the spatial data produced by the Caribbean Handbook on Risk Information Management project for five Eastern Caribbean and Central American countries. Contents: 179 layers listed on the home page on 29 September 2026, including coastal flood depth grids for Belize under hurricane categories 1 to 5, national flood and flash flood hazard maps for Dominica, landslide inventories (such as the UNOSAT mapping after Tropical Storm Erika in 2015) and landslide susceptibility, 10 m digital elevation models, land cover and OpenStreetMap-derived building footprints used as elements at risk, plus road and critical facility layers described in the project's data management book. Producer: the CHARIM consortium led by the University of Twente for the World Bank, with national agencies as layer owners. Coverage: Belize, Dominica, Grenada, Saint Lucia and Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, mostly national scale, prepared around 2015 to 2016. Format and access: each layer page offers downloads as zipped Shapefile, GeoJSON, CSV, KML or GeoTIFF, and metadata as ISO 19139, Dublin Core or FGDC; the companion charim.net site gives PDF maps and hazard reports per country. Free; no licence is stated on the layer pages. Caveats: the GeoNode API and OGC capabilities endpoints redirect to the home page, so layers must be browsed one by one; the data are from the project period and not maintained since. Simulation uses: hazard layers and assets for flood and landslide exposure analysis, road and shelter planning, and cost-benefit studies in small island states. Related records: none yet in the main catalogue; a Dominica building height and roof material dataset from Roseau is under review on another branch.
